title: Efficiency: per-write kmalloc for copy_from_user bounce buffer
description: crypto2dev_fd.c:crypto2dev_fd_write — every write() allocates a fresh kernel buffer (kmalloc(count)), copies user data into it, then releases it after update() returns. For a workload that calls write() in 4KB chunks over a 1MB payload, this is 256 kmalloc/kfree pairs per operation. This is correct (copy_from_user cannot be done under a mutex; pre-copying is required), but the allocation could be replaced by reusing the inbuf or a per-session bounce buffer sized to the session's typical chunk. This is a micro-optimization and only matters at very high throughput (>10K writes/sec). Not worth changing now; document for future profiling.
close_reason: Confirmed not worth changing per description: micro-optimization only matters at >10K writes/sec which is not a current concern
